inlines.v: OR'NAMENT, noun [Latin ornamentum, from orno, to adorn. Varro informs us that this was primitively osnamentum; but this is improbable. See Adorn.] 1. That which embellishes; something which, added to another thing, renders it more beautiful to the eye. The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers, the bonnets and the ornaments of the legs - Isaiah 3:18. 2. In architecture, ornaments are sculpture or carved work. 3. Embellishment; decoration; additional beauty. - The ornament of a meek and quiet spirit which is in the sight of God of great price. 1 Peter 3:4. OR'NAMENT, verb transitive To adorn; to deck; to embellish.
